articles.title: Rugby League World Cup: Jon Wilkin says tournament format is 'fundamentally flawed' as England on brink of historic exit
articles.summary: England are teetering on the brink of a historic group-stage exit at the Rugby League World Cup despite beating Papua New Guinea on Friday; England need Tonga to defeat Samoa by more than 46 points to advance to the knockout stages
articles.body:
England sealed a 34-12 victory against Papua New Guinea on Friday but needed to win by a margin of 68 points to give themselves a chance of leapfrogging Samoa in Pool B and C and advancing to the semi-finals on points difference.

Now their hopes rest on Tonga, who face off against Samoa on Sunday. England need Tonga to win by more than 46 points to secure a spot in the knockout stages.

The new tournament structure, which has been downsized from 16 teams to 10, came after Australia stepped in as hosts following France's withdrawal in 2023 for financial reasons.

It has effectively meant that each group game in Pool B and C has carried more jeopardy than before.

"Australia have done a great job to organise a tournament in such a short space of time, but it was fundamentally flawed, unfair in the extreme to the start," Wilkin said.

"The actual competition structure is just diabolical. England were dealt an incredibly difficult task, because they essentially played their quarter-final in week one."

The tournament has two pools, one featuring four teams - Australia, New Zealand, Cook Islands and Fiji - and the other featuring six teams.

England were drawn in the second group, Pool B and C, alongside Tonga, Samoa, Papua New Guinea, Lebanon and France.

The top two teams from each group qualify for the knockout rounds, and in the event of a tie, teams are judged on their head-to-head record before points difference.

Brian McDermott's side were beaten in their first match, a 30-12 defeat to Tonga, which put their hopes of qualifying in the balance, despite later thrashing France by 82 points in round two.

"England knew after their loss against Tonga that it was all going to be about points difference, and [qualifying] was going to be incredibly difficult," Wilkin said. "I think the structure and the setup of the competition was done in short notice.

"I think the International Rugby League, who set up this tournament, have done an incredible job to get it on and actually and get in a position where we can have the tournament.

"So, I commend them for that, but I just think the tournament structure is laughable. Like, no quarter-finals? There's a number of ways you could have manufactured or engineered a quarter-finals situation.

"England should be in the quarter-finals, of the World Cup. They had a disappointing 30-40 minutes against Tonga, and they're out."

Wilkin questions England's preparations but backs McDermott

Wilkin backed McDermott to stay on as England head coach, but added he needed a new structure around him while questioning the decision to arrive in Australia just over a week before the tournament.

McDermott revealed earlier in October that the side had taken a convoluted route to reach their Perth base, flying from the north of England to Singapore first and then to Sydney, before travelling to Western Australia.

"England knew they were playing in the World Cup," Wilkin said. "England knew the structure. England knew they needed to win the first game.

"How it is possible to fly your athletes out, economy class, to Singapore, to Sydney, then back to Perth, jet-lagged, and then expect to play against the NRL-standard Tonga team week one and produce a performance is laughable.

"It's a laughable logistical mess that again isn't elite. Nothing elite about it. In any other elite sport it's like, 'no stone unturned', and I just don't think England had that going into this World Cup.

"I think McDermott is an exceptional coach. I'd give him more time, but there needs to be some management and structure behind him to those things right.

"You know, those things really matter, and a jet-lagged team going into play a Tongan team who are rife with stars was fundamentally where it went wrong."

articles.title: Mikel Arteta warns Max Dowman 'we are not in Disneyland' after red card against Fleetwood
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta says "we are not in Disneyland" and that he will hold Max Dowman to the same standards as other first-team players after the teenager's red card against Fleetwood.
articles.body:
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has told Max Dowman "we are not in Disneyland" and that he intends to hold the teenager to the same standards as other first-team players.

Dowman, 16, was sent off in the 85th minute of Arsenal's penalty shoot-out loss to Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday after reacting to a heavy challenge by Harrison Neal and will serve a three-match ban .

A visibly annoyed Arteta spoke to Dowman as the teenager left the pitch, and on Friday spoke about the incident for the first time, saying he warned the attacker before the game about dealing with provocation.

"I haven't seen the reaction to my reaction, whether it is positive or negative. But you need to understand the context and the relationship that I have with him and what we discussed just before we went out," Arteta said of his words to Dowman.

"But, I don't know. You can have another reaction. If you see the reaction of my father and my mother with me some days you might say 'I don't like the reaction'. For me, it was the best reaction to be who I am."

Arteta revealed that he had spoken to Dowman on Thursday and said there were "no issues at all" between the pair. However, he added that he needs to be "very straight" with Dowman and clear of the standards expected.

Dowman was sent off for the England U19s earlier this month where he was also on the end of heavy challenges in a match with the United States.

Of that red card, Arteta said: "They are his age. They are 16 – the same. What is the reaction? That is the level and that is the reaction.

"And whether it is right or wrong, that is the reaction."

Arteta also spoke of the impact the red card had on the team, saying: "And the reaction when I don't win, you want to know what my reaction is? I am [angry] big time.

"So, we need to be ready for that. This is the environment and this is the reality, otherwise we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League and this level.

"We look after him so much that you cannot imagine.

"But at the same time we are going to demand from him, like everybody else, because he needs to earn the right to play. Because the other boys, what are they going to tell me? You need to be fair."

The Gunners did appeal against the red card but the Football Association (FA) upheld the decision. Of that, Arteta said he was "very disappointed", adding "we are lucky today that he (Dowman) hasn't had a broken foot."

articles.title: Thieves smash Munich air disaster memorial display case and steal treasured items honouring eight Man Utd players
articles.summary: A memorial dedicated to the victims of the 1958 Munich air disaster, including eight Manchester United players, has been vandalized, with thieves stealing significant memorabilia. The emotional impact on families and supporters is profound as the connection between Manchester and Munich endures.
articles.body: For nearly seven decades, Manchester and Munich have shared a connection forged by one of football's darkest tragedies, with a memorial at the site of the 1958 air disaster serving as a place of remembrance for families and supporters. That memorial has now been targeted by thieves, who smashed a glass display case and removed treasured items commemorating the 23 people who lost their lives.Thieves break into Munich memorial display caseA glass sculpture and several medals have been stolen from a memorial commemorating the victims of the Munich air disaster, including eight Manchester United players, after criminals broke into a display case at Manchesterplatz in Munich.According to Munich Police, the glass was smashed using a stone, with the theft believed to have taken place between 08:00 and 13:00 local time on Monday, October 26. The Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation (MMMF), which helps preserve the site and its history, confirmed that the display had been damaged and that some of its memorabilia remained missing.Among the stolen objects was a glass sculpture originally presented to Munich's former mayor, Dieter Reiter. Mark Salzmann, chairman of Red Docs Munich, a Bayern Munich supporters' group involved in caring for the memorial, said the exact number of missing medals was still unclear.According to the BBC, Salzmann's mother discovered the damage while driving past the memorial, after which members of the group began assessing what had been taken. Red Docs Munich regularly collects tributes left by visitors from around the world and places selected items inside the display case, making the theft particularly distressing for those who have helped maintain the memorial.Foundation chair says theft has hurt familiesIfty Ahmed, chairman of the Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation, said the incident had caused considerable emotional distress to families who lost relatives in the disaster, explaining that the memorial had become a place where they could find solace.Speaking to BBC News, Ahmed said: "They don't understand the damage that they've caused."He also made clear that the stolen objects could not erase the memories associated with the memorial, adding: "And whatever they've taken from inside the showcase, they haven't taken our memories."In a statement issued on Thursday, October 29, Ahmed said:"The Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation is deeply saddened by this act of vandalism and theft."Manchesterplatz is a place of enormous significance to the families of the 23 people who lost their lives as a result of the Munich Air Disaster, and to Manchester United supporters across the world."We are particularly grateful to our friends in Munich, especially the Red Docs, for their continued care and dedication to this very special place, and for acting so swiftly to repair the damage."Those responsible may have damaged a display case and stolen treasured items, but they cannot steal our memories, diminish our friendship or destroy the legacy of those we remember. Their memory will endure, and the bond between Manchester and Munich will remain unbreakable."Manchester United and rival supporters offer supportThe foundation confirmed that the broken glass was replaced on the same day as the incident, although several commemorative objects have yet to be recovered. Manchester United offered to cover the repair costs, but Ahmed said the foundation had already agreed to meet the expense itself.The response has also extended beyond Manchester United's own supporters, with Ahmed revealing that fans of Liverpool, Manchester City and Leeds United had sent messages of support following the theft.Salzmann said the objects inside the display were unique and could not easily be replaced, although Red Docs Munich and the foundation were discussing possible replacements.The foundation has urged those responsible to return the stolen objects, which hold considerable sentimental value for the families and supporters who visit the site.What happened in the 1958 Munich air disaster?The memorial commemorates the Munich air disaster of February 6, 1958, when a British European Airways Flight 609 crashed during take-off at Munich-Riem Airport after refuelling on its return from a European Cup match against Red Star Belgrade in Yugoslavia.The crash claimed 23 lives, including eight Manchester United players and three members of the club's staff. Among the footballers killed were club captain Roger Byrne, England internationals Tommy Taylor and Duncan Edwards, alongside Geoff Bent, Eddie Colman, Mark Jones, David Pegg and Billy Whelan.The tragedy devastated a Manchester United side managed by Matt Busby, whose young team had become known as the Busby Babes. Several players survived the crash, including Bobby Charlton, who would later become one of the most celebrated figures in English football.Manchesterplatz has remained an important place of remembrance for the victims and their families. A memorial stone was installed there in 2004, while the glass display case was added in 2020 and officially inaugurated in 2023.The annual remembrance service continues to attract supporters and visitors from around the world, with approximately 1,500 people attending the February ceremony this year, according to the foundation.Salzmann said the support received following the theft reflected the enduring relationship between the two cities, adding that the connection between Manchester and Munich "will never go away."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Isco, la jugada de córner del Málaga
articles.standfirst: Funes desvela que una jugada ensayada lleva el nombre del mediapunta, rival este sábado
articles.summary: Funes desvela que una jugada ensayada malaguista lleva el nombre del mediapunta
articles.body: El duelo del sábado ante el Real Betis tendrá un componente especial para el Málaga CF. Además de tratarse del primer derbi andaluz de la temporada, el conjunto blanquiazul se reencontrará con dos figuras que forman parte de su historia reciente: Manuel Pellegrini e Isco. Ambos fueron protagonistas de una de las etapas más brillantes de la entidad, con la clasificación para la Champions League como punto culminante. La conexión con aquella generación también permanece dentro del vestuario malaguista. Juanfran Funes desveló este viernes una curiosa tradición que se mantiene desde su etapa en el filial y que tiene precisamente a Isco como protagonista. "En el filial, a nuestros córneres les poníamos nombres de jugadores del Málaga porque queríamos trabajar nuestra señal de identidad. Uno de nuestros córneres se llamó Isco. Cuando llegué al primer equipo lo seguimos haciendo. Nuestros jugadores continúan llamándolo Isco", explicó el técnico. Una buena parte de la plantilla ya conoce al Betis de cerca después de medirse al conjunto verdiblanco en el Trofeo Costa del Sol del pasado curso. Aquel encuentro terminó con triunfo malaguista por 3-1 y este sábado algunos de aquellos futbolistas volverán a encontrarse con Isco, aunque esta vez con tres puntos en juego y en un escenario tan especial como La Cartuja. Así, una de las jugadas de estrategia que el Málaga lleva tiempo preparando podría tener un significado añadido este sábado: el córner "Isco" frente al propio Isco.

articles.title: Tottenham: James Maddison available to face Crystal Palace, says De Zerbi
articles.summary: Tottenham midfielder James Maddison is available to face Crystal Palace on Saturday says manager Roberto De Zerbi, despite an injury scare last week.
articles.body:
Tottenham midfielder James Maddison is available to face Crystal Palace on Saturday despite an injury scare last week, manager Roberto De Zerbi says.

The 29-year-old England international limped off in the 51st minute of Spurs' 2-0 victory at Chelsea.

It sparked worries about Maddison's fitness, after he missed the majority of last season with an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury.

Maddison then fractured his shoulder in Tottenham 's opening weekend defeat at Brentford this season, before returning to the starting line-up earlier this month when he scored a spectacular goal in a 3-1 win against Coventry.

When asked about Maddison's condition, De Zerbi said he will be "available" for the visit of Palace.

"This week he didn't work like the other players, but for tomorrow he is available and he is a special player for us," said De Zerbi.

"For James Maddison or the players who are coming from a long injury, they have to work more than the other players, but he has already four or five weeks - he is working very hard and consistently.

"So, I think it's not a problem if he loses two days [training], but then we have to analyse if we take the risk or not."

Tottenham have beaten Coventry and Chelsea since Maddison's return to the starting line-up, with the club 14th in the Premier League after climbing out of the relegation zone.

Maddison joined Tottenham from Leicester City in 2023 on a five-year contract in a deal worth £40m.

He's scored 17 goals and provided 21 assists in 85 appearances for the north London club.

articles.body: El Johnstone Burgh, equipo de la quinta división escocesa, tendrá que jugar dos partidos a al vez después de que haya sido "imposible" reprogramarlos a otra fecha. El conjunto escocés se enfrentará al Tayport, en la Copa de Comunidades de Escocia el sábado 21 de noviembre a las 14:00 hora del Reino Unido, y al Dunipace, en la Copa de la Liga, media hora después y a 90 kilómetros de distancia. El Johnstone ha explicado en un comunicado que ha tratado por todos los modos de cambiar la fecha de alguno de los partidos, pero que sus rivales se han negado para mantener el horario del sábado. "No ha sido por falta de esfuerzo. Incluso nos hemos ofrecido a dar nuestra parte de la taquilla para cubrir cualquier molestia que pueda ocasionar cambiar el partido". Para solventar esta papeleta, el Johnstone tendrá que alinear a dos equipos diferentes o no presentarse a alguno de los dos encuentros, con las consecuencias que ello acarrea.

articles.title: Ex-football chief admits offences linked to woman's drugging and rape by husband
articles.summary: Karl Lindsay resigned from non-league Taunton Town Football Club in Somerset before he was charged.
articles.body:
A former football club chief executive has pleaded guilty to offences relating to the drugging and raping of a woman by her husband and others.

Karl Lindsay, 56, who resigned from non-league Taunton Town Football Club in Somerset before he was charged, has admitted the offences, which happened between 2015 and 2025.

Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court heard Lindsay's offending related to the rape of the woman by her husband and others in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester, and the administration of substances to stupefy her for the purpose of sexual acts.

The woman's husband, who is in his 60s and cannot be named to protect his wife's anonymity, has already admitted 62 offences against his wife, including rape.

The woman at the centre of the case was in court with one of her relatives and watched Lindsay intently as he entered his guilty pleas.

Three other men, Keith Fotheringham, 59, from Dundee, Scotland, Sean Peers, 38, from Stockport, and Graham Brougham, 74, from Northwich, have already admitted sexually abusing her at previous hearings.

The trial of nine other defendants accused of sexual offences against the woman has been scheduled to start on Monday after a series of delays.

The men are all alleged to have committed offences between 2015 and 2025.

articles.summary: Así queda definitivamente constituida la Comisión Delegada, junto a Sevilla, Barcelona, Real Madrid, Betis, Alavés y Villarreal
articles.body: Real Sporting de Gijón, Celta de Vigo Fortuna, Real Oviedo, Leganés, Las Palmas y Almería han resultado elegidos como representantes de LaLiga Hypermotion para la Comisión Delegada de LaLiga, anunció este viernes el organismo. Con la elección de estos seis clubes ha quedado definitivamente constituida la Comisión Delegada, de la que también forman parte Sevilla, Barcelona, Real Madrid, Real Betis, Deportivo Alavés y Villarreal, como los representantes de LaLiga EA Sports, explicó en un comunicado. Como vicepresidente primero se mantiene el consejero delegado del Atlético de Madrid, Miguel Ángel Gil Marín, y como vicepresidente segundo, el consejero del Eibar, Ion Ander Ulzaia, que quedaron designados directamente hace dos semanas sin necesidad de votación, tras ser las únicas candidaturas presentadas. Tampoco fue necesario votar los miembros de la Comisión Delegada en representación de LaLiga Sports, al coincidir el número de candidaturas presentadas con las seis plazas que le corresponden, mientras que los de la LaLiga Hypermotion sí que tuvieron que votarse, al ser superior el número de candidaturas presentadas al de puestos a cubrir. La Comisión Delegada de LaLiga es el órgano de gobierno y administración ordinaria que se convoca y celebra obligatoriamente con carácter mensual, durante la competición, y con carácter extraordinario cuando así lo soliciten, al menos, cuatro de sus miembros o el presidente del organismo. El mandato de sus miembros es de dos años y puede ser renovado por periodos sucesivos de igual duración.

articles.title: Maxence Lacroix could be out until January for Chelsea
articles.summary: Chelsea fear Maxence Lacroix will have a lengthy lay-off having suffered a serious hamstring injury.
articles.body:
Chelsea fear defender Maxence Lacroix is set for a lengthy lay-off after suffering a serious hamstring injury.

Multiple sources have told BBC Sport that the France international, 26, could be out until January, meaning he could miss up to 10 matches.

The setback occurred at the end of the first half of Wednesday's Carabao Cup loss to Liverpool on penalties, as Lacroix sprinted and attempted to block a shot.

Sources inside Chelsea , including manager Xabi Alonso, have been guarded on the length of the absence.

When asked about Lacroix's injury at his media conference before Saturday's Premier League visit of Manchester United , Alonso said: "Max, he picked up an injury, and we expect that he's not going to be ready before the international break. So he will be a few weeks out."

The injury is a blow for Alonso, who has started his £52m summer signing from Crystal Palace in all but one of Chelsea 's 11 matches across all competitions this season.

Only attacker Morgan Rogers has played more than Lacroix for Chelsea this season.

The Blues have a six-man centre-back group featuring Levi Colwill, Wesley Fofana, Josh Acheampong, Jorrel Hato and Aaron Anselmino as alternatives, although the latter two are also currently injured, with others having also lined up at full-back.

Asked about the potential replacements, Alonso added: "With Max's injury, we have Wes, we have Levi [Colwill], Josh [Acheampong], he could play as well as centre-back.

"Jorrel when he is back with the team [is an option]. Wes has played [and] even if he missed the penalty [in the shootout], I think that he had a good game.

"He was consistent, he was strong and I saw many positives from his performance. We know the level that he has had and he's going to be important."

Alonso also revealed that goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez is having a special mask fitted to play while recovering from a broken jaw and midfielder Moises Caicedo avoided injury despite concerns after the midweek clash with Liverpool .

Chelsea are fifth in the Premier League with 13 points from eight matches, but have kept only one clean sheet in that period.

articles.title: Eddie Howe to Man Utd? The fans, the finances, the football structure
articles.summary: Eddie Howe is being linked with the Manchester United job, but what are some of the considerations for him and the club?
articles.body:
When Sir Jim Ratcliffe became a co-owner of Manchester United in 2024, much of the narrative centred on his desire to rebuild the club around a British core.

Given the expense of buying homegrown players, and the difficulties Michael Carrick - the first permanent British managerial appointment of the Ineos era - has faced this season, perhaps Ratcliffe is rethinking.

But if Carrick fails to stop the rot and loses his job, United are already considering the merits of appointing another British coach - albeit one who is more experienced.

That Eddie Howe is a contender for a job that remains one of the most high-profile in world football isn't hard to fathom.

Speak to those who have worked alongside Howe and they describe a man whose track record of improving players is a direct result of his relentless approach on the training field.

They will also tell you Howe is someone who places an unwavering importance on the methodology of setting a winning culture.

Howe may lack experience at one of the traditional top-six clubs, but his body of work at Bournemouth and Newcastle is impressive.

Having been appointed Bournemouth boss with the club facing relegation from League Two in January 2009, Howe led them to the Premier League in 2015. He went on to establish the Cherries as a top-flight club before leaving - for a second time - in 2020.

In 2021, Howe was appointed Newcastle manager. He led them from relegation trouble to qualification for the Champions League on two occasions and won the EFL Cup - the club's first trophy in 56 years - in 2025.

Man Utd stick with Carrick - inside a turbulent 48 hours at Old Trafford

Of course, managing Manchester United is an altogether different proposition.

Indeed, Howe's emergence as a potential successor to Carrick has been greeted with negativity in some circles.

Sections of the fanbase have been vocal on social media with their opinion that Howe isn't a big enough name to replace Carrick.

Former United players Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt also fell short of providing their backing to Howe on their podcast, though it is worth pointing out they spoke in favour of the 48-year-old's potential appointment when Ruben Amorim was sacked in January.

Ex-captain Roy Keane is among those to have backed Howe as a possible successor to Carrick, and other former top-flight players - including Darren Bent, Gareth Barry and Jack Wilshere - have also touted him as the man for the job.

Of course, if you look hard enough you'll find voices for and against every potential manager, and it will be up to United chief executive Omar Berrada, sporting director Jason Wilcox and director of recruitment Christopher Vivell to weigh up how they proceed.

Their first decision will be what happens with Carrick, and Saturday's match against Chelsea is likely to have a bearing on how United move forward.

If Carrick does depart, finances will inevitably be a factor.

The former Middlesbrough boss and his staff will need to be paid up before United even get to factoring in the monetary commitment towards their next head coach.

While the details of Howe's agreement with Newcastle when he left in the summer remain confidential, it is understood that as things stand any club or national team would be required to pay a seven-figure compensation fee to the Magpies.

Multiple sources have told BBC Sport that Newcastle - with a view to protecting themselves against Howe walking straight into another club - reached an agreement over a compensation structure that decreases over time.

It is understood that figure started at £6m but has already reduced by half.

The compensation payments have an expiry date - understood to be before the end of the season - at which point he can be appointed for nothing.

Of course, in an industry in which astronomical figures are the norm, the prospect of paying a maximum of £3m for Howe may not be too problematic.

That said, given the amount Manchester United have spent on hiring and firing managers in recent years, it is understandable if Berrada and Wilcox want to keep costs down.

How talking about Man Utd's cycle of doom became an industry

Would Howe fit Man Utd's footballing structure?

As well as the doubts from some supporters about Howe's potential appointment, there has also been conjecture over how he would fit in United's footballing structure.

At both Bournemouth and Newcastle, Howe developed a strong powerbase in all aspects of the footballing department - including recruitment.

That dynamic wasn't without financial benefit to Howe's employers.

The likes of Nathan Ake, Callum Wilson and Tyrone Mings were all signed by Howe at Bournemouth - and sold for a big profit by the Cherries.

At Newcastle, meanwhile, Howe was instrumental in the signings of Bruno Guimarares, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Alexander Isak - all of whom were sold for more than they joined for. Dan Burn, Lewis Hall and Tino Livramento are among those to have developed into full England internationals under his coaching.

But with a football management structure at Old Trafford that includes Berrada, Wilcox and Vivell, it is likely that Howe - at least not immediately - would not be afforded the same level of autonomy.

Howe, though, is on record saying he is happy to work alongside sporting directors, and has a track record of doing so - firstly at Bournemouth under Richard Hughes, then chief executive Neill Blake.

At Newcastle, he worked closely with senior management figures Dan Ashworth, Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi - so fitting into Manchester United's structure wouldn't be drastically different.

Whether he would want the job given the challenges, we may never know. And ultimately it is the opinion of Manchester United's decision-makers that will truly matter.

'An obvious contender to replace Carrick' - analysis

Howe is an obvious contender for the Manchester United job, just as he would be if the England head coach's position became available.

Whether he is offered it or not will give a clear indication about the path United are going down.

Director of football Jason Wilcox is thought to favour the 48-year-old, with director of recruitment Christopher Vivell preferring former Bayern Munich and Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann.

Ultimately, their recommendations will be assessed by chief executive Omar Berrada, with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and co-chairs Joel and Avram Glazer having the final say.

It is not completely clear where the negativity about Howe moving to Old Trafford comes from, other than Wilcox being targeted by Manchester United fans during the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth.

In the current managerial climate, few managers get the chance to build a body at work at one club over a number of years as, for instance, Sir Alex Ferguson did at Aberdeen before he moved south in November 1986.

There is clearly a general disillusionment among the club's matchgoing fans around the football decisions taken since Ratcliffe bought his minority stake in early 2024, but Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick have all been backed.

Some say no manager can succeed at United with the structure as it is, and it is clear whoever is in charge needs to mould together a squad bought by six permanent managers, most of whom have differing playing styles.

articles.title: Michael Carrick: What Man Utd boss could change for Saturday's Premier League game at Chelsea
articles.summary: Michael Carrick remains in charge at Manchester United despite going eight games without a win; William Bitibiri and Callum Bishop discuss what Carrick could change to revive his fortunes ahead of Saturday's Premier League trip to Chelsea
articles.body:
A run of eight games without a win has left Carrick searching for answers, with the performances raising as many questions as the results.

The energy and organisation of his interim spell last season has been replaced by a team struggling to find their identity.

Chelsea away is next on Saturday. Carrick needs to find solutions, and quickly. But what can he actually change?

Stop the high press and make United harder to play through

One of the biggest problems facing Carrick is that Manchester United are making life too easy for their opponents.

The intention to be more aggressive out of possession is understandable, but the execution has been off. United have repeatedly been pulled out of position, with gaps opening between the forward line and midfield that opponents have exploited to progress through the centre or find space out wide.

United are among the Premier League's most frequent users of a high block, employing it for 36 per cent of opposition build-up phases. Only Tottenham and Liverpool have used it more often, with Manchester City level with United.

But pressing high is one thing, making it work is another. United have won the ball high up the pitch 52 times this season, but only 10 of those occasions have led to a shot. They have yet to score from one.

Defeats to Atletico Madrid and Como exposed those weaknesses. United's attempts to press have lacked the coordination and intensity required to make the approach effective, leaving defenders exposed when the first line is bypassed.

Bruno Fernandes questioned the decision not to press man to man against Como, arguing that opponents were being given too much time to build attacks. But the answer is not necessarily to press higher and harder. United must first establish a structure they can execute consistently.

There were encouraging signs against Leeds, when Carrick's side looked more disciplined and compact, even if they could not turn a 1-1 draw into victory.

There is also a wider issue with United's defensive shape. They have spent just 56.5 minutes in a high defensive compactness structure this season, the 18th-lowest figure in the Premier League.

A similar approach to the Leeds game at Chelsea would make sense. United need shorter distances between their defensive and midfield lines, better protection in central areas and a clearer understanding of when to engage.

Until United can defend as a unit, their tactical confusion will continue.

Fernandes must return to the starting XI

Leaving Fernandes on the bench against Bournemouth was a significant decision, particularly after the captain questioned United's tactics following the Champions League defeat to Como.

Carrick insisted it was a football decision, but the midfielder's absence was impossible to ignore as United suffered another damaging defeat. Fernandes was not even introduced as the situation deteriorated, leaving questions over whether the decision was based purely on performance or also reflected a power play from Carrick.

The clear-the-air talks between the pair this week appear to have drawn a line under the disagreement. Carrick has reiterated that Fernandes remains captain and said the club can move forward together.

There is no guarantee Fernandes alone can transform United's fortunes. His own performances have not consistently reached the levels of last season, and the team cannot continue relying on individual quality to compensate for collective shortcomings.

However, he remains one of United's most influential players, capable of creating chances, progressing possession and providing the decisive pass in transition. When he is on song, his ability to connect midfield and attack is particularly important when United struggle to break down organised defences.

Carrick needs his best players on the pitch, especially when results are this poor. If Fernandes is fit and ready, leaving him out again would be difficult to justify.

What is ironic about Manchester United's recent struggles is that the senior players Carrick relied on during his impressive interim spell last season are now struggling to deliver the same levels of performance.

Fernandes must return to the starting XI but reinstating the captain should not mean ignoring the youngsters who could inject some much-needed energy into a team that has looked short of intensity and conviction.

Harry Amass impressed during pre-season and deserves an opportunity to compete for a place at left-back. With United struggling to find consistency in that position, there is a case for giving the youngster a chance to show what he can offer.

Shea Lacey is another option. The 19-year-old has had limited opportunities since scoring in the Carabao Cup against Brighton, but has shown the enthusiasm and willingness to take responsibility that United have lacked at times.

Introducing young players is not a solution to every problem, and throwing them into a struggling side comes with its own risks. But if experienced players are not delivering, Carrick must be willing to look elsewhere.

Fernandes can provide the quality to complement that youthful energy. United need a balance of experience and enthusiasm - and Carrick should not be afraid to give the next generation an opportunity to make their mark.

Go back to basics and stop moving players around

Man Utd this season appear to be spending as much time adapting to new positions as they are trying to find form.

Diogo Dalot has operated at both right-back and left-back, while Leny Yoro has been used at right-back as well as centre-back. Mason Mount has featured on the right, and Youri Tielemans, previously viewed as a deeper-lying midfielder, has recently been pushed into more advanced positions.

Further forward, Matheus Cunha has been asked to operate from the left and through the middle, while Bryan Mbeumo has predominantly featured on the right despite producing some of his best football centrally last season.

Players out of position? Square pegs in round holes? How familiar does that sound?

There are understandable reasons for some of these changes, including injuries and the need to find a winning combination. But the constant reshuffling has made it difficult for United to establish consistent partnerships and give players a settled understanding of their roles.

Carrick's willingness to experiment was one of the positives of his interim spell, especially in the transition away from what Ruben Amorim was often critiqued for.

Against Chelsea, he needs to identify the strongest available XI and give players the best opportunity to perform in positions that suit them. That does not mean abandoning tactical adjustments, but United need a reliable foundation before they can start building something more ambitious.

articles.summary: Lamine Yamal was tipped for the Golden Ball which went to Harry Kane, but his Barca boss ‘proud’ of teenager’s reaction.
articles.body:
Lamine Yamal has “reacted very well” following the disappointment of the Ballon d’Or being awarded to Harry Kane, Barcelona coach Hansi Flick said on Friday.

Despite winning La Liga with the Catalan club and lifting the World Cup with Spain , the 19-year-old winger came third in the vote for the best player in the world on Monday, behind Kane and Kylian Mbappe.

“Harry Kane deserved it, but you already know what I think about Lamine. He’s at the level required to win this award,” Flick said ahead of the La Liga leaders’ home match against Alaves.

“I’m very proud of Lamine. He reacted very well and was very focused in training.

“That’s the way to respond. His mentality is very good for the team.”

Yamal will have a chance to put any lingering disappointment behind him on Saturday when Barcelona look to correct course at home to Alaves following two high-profile defeats.

After winning their first 11 matches in all competitions, Barcelona were flying but then came undone when they travelled to PSG in the Champions League last Tuesday.

That 4-2 reverse in the French capital was swiftly followed by a Mbappe-inspired 2-1 loss at home to Real Madrid in La Liga last weekend.

“The most important thing tomorrow is to win,” Flick said.

“The team is playing well and we believe in our strengths. I’ve seen a good training session and a positive mood. We have to show that tomorrow.

“Alaves are a team that know how to defend well, but we’re Barca and we want to show our best version.”

Barcelona still hold a two-point lead at the top of La Liga ahead of their meeting with Atletico Madrid.

While the German coach admitted he does not like losing, he insisted that the campaign is “a long road”.

“It’s at the end of the season that we can win trophies,” he added.

“We have to deal with it. We could have won, but we have to accept defeat and learn from it.”

articles.title: Brian Fariñas, el joven medio al que Flick medita hacer debutar... de lateral
articles.standfirst: Ha sido citado en nueve encuentros y aún no se ha estrenado, pero podría hacerlo mañana
articles.summary: Ha sido citado en nueve encuentros y aún no se ha estrenado, pero podría hacerlo mañana
articles.body: Brian Fariñas. Centrocampista. 20 años. Llegó a La Masía hace nueve temporadas procedente del fútbol base del Villarreal. Este curso, es uno de los jugadores de la cantera al que Hansi Flick ha subido. Tiene dorsal de la primera plantilla, luce el 4, y ha sido citado en nueve encuentros pero no ha debutado. Podría hacerlo mañana contra el Alavés, moviéndose, además, en una posición que no es la suya. Otro joven más que se gana al técnico culé. El jugador de Benicarló llegó al fútbol base azulgrana en julio de 2018: se sumó como infantil de primer año. Fue creciendo en la cantera y se convirtió en una pieza clave en el triplete (Liga, Copa y UEFA Youth League) del Juvenil A en el curso 2024-25. Debutó con el Barça Atlètic en la temporada 2023-24 (el 16 de marzo del 2024 en la victoria en el campo del Teruel). Aquel curso participó con el filial en dos partidos, y la siguiente temporada, aún siendo juvenil, jugó siete encuentros. En la 25-26, con Belletti en el banquillo del segundo equipo culé, Fariñas se convierte en una pieza clave del Barça Atlètic: interviene en 35 cruces, en los que marca 5 goles y reparte 6 asistencias. Esa gran campaña del versátil medio, que tiene contrato hasta junio de 2028, provoca que Flick se fije en él y se lo lleva a realizar la pretemporada con el primer equipo. Ya no volvería a bajar al Barça Atlètic. Convence al técnico y se gana un dorsal en la élite. Suyo es el 4 del Barcelona. Brian ha sido citado en nueve encuentros esta temporada, seis de LaLiga (contra el Elche, el Athletic, el Rayo, el Getafe, el Betis y el Real Madrid) y los tres de la Champions League (frente a Feyenoord, Galatasaray y PSG), pero aún no se ha estrenado. Puede hacerlo muy pronto. En cuestión de horas: mañana contra el Alavés en el cruce de la jornada 11 de LaLiga que se disputa en el Spotify Camp Nou. "Jules Koundé está fuera, también Espart, Eric, Christensen... nos faltan cuatro atrás. Hay que buscar soluciones, y en eso estamos", comentó este viernes Hansi Flick. "Brian es muy inteligente. Se entrena con nosotros desde el inicio de temporada. Hace un trabajo fantástico. Se merece jugar ya", añadió, tajante, el preparador culé. Y de estrenarse, lo haría, a priori, como lateral derecho y no como centrocampista. Ya jugó en pretemporada en el ala de la zaga, contra el Birmingham City, y su rendimiento dejó satisfecho al preparador. Así, Fariñas está a punto de sumarse a la amplia lista de canteranos que han subido a la elite con Flick. El preparador culé ya ha dado la alternativa, entre otros, a Bernal, Gerard Martín, Andrés Cuenca, Jofre Torrents, Dro, Tommy Marqués, Xavi Espart... su confianza en el talento azulgrana es máxima.

articles.title: El creador del meme de Mbappé: "Estaba planeando un viaje a China, espero que no tengan nada contra mí"
articles.standfirst: Younes Khelifi, francés de 28 años, atiende a MARCA para explicar la intrahistoria del fenómeno que acabó enfrentando al jugador del Madrid con el país asiático
articles.summary: Younes Khelifi, francés de 28 años, atiende a MARCA para explicar la intrahistoria del fenómeno que acabó enfrentando al jugador del Madrid con el país asiático
articles.body: Younes Khelifi programa por oficio, sigue al fútbol por devoción y gestiona en 'X' la cuenta Frenchaicovers, donde cocina deepfakes e inteligencia artificial en clave de humor. De ahí salió, en el verano de 2023, el montaje que años después incendiaría las relaciones entre Kylian Mbappé y China. El origen lo explica él en MARCA: “En aquel momento había rumores sobre la salida de Mbappé del PSG y parecía que tenía bajo su control a la presidencia. Cuando anunciaron su continuidad, me vino a la cabeza la imagen de Mbappé como líder supremo del club. Con los aficionados solíamos cantar la famosa canción Red Sun in the Sky en el coche, por diversión. Así que decidí conectar a Mbappé con Mao Zedong de forma automática”. Nunca imaginó el alcance. “Era solo una broma sobre la actualidad. Jamás pensé que pudiera salir de Francia, sinceramente”, nos relata. Pero salió, y el vídeo se repostearía partido tras partido durante tres años. Lo primero que supo del éxito fue que el propio futbolista lo enseñaba a sus compañeros, y lejos de molestarle, le encantó: “Me puso muy contento que lo conociera. Es un chico joven como yo, que se ríe de todo. Tiene un trabajo, vale, pero también es una persona, así que puede bromear sobre cualquier cosa, incluso sobre sí mismo. No me sorprendió”. La broma dejó de serlo cuando estalló la polémica con China, y la primera reacción de Khelifi fue de puro vértigo. “La primera hora, cuando me desperté y me enteré, sí que me cuestioné si debía buscarme un abogado para defenderme, quizá frente al clan Mbappé o frente a LaLiga. Pero supongo que soy demasiado pequeño para defenderme”. El susto le duró lo que tardó en pensarlo dos veces: “Después de una buena hora me dije que estaba todo bien. No creo que hiciera nada malo, porque nunca quise herir a los chinos ni a Mbappé. Era solo una broma que estaba causando tantas consecuencias en lo económico, en lo geopolítico… Sé que no tengo nada que perder”. Hacia el futbolista solo guarda compasión, y la explica con una lectura que mezcla la cultura francesa y el malentendido. “Creo que lo lamenta profundamente. Cuando ves el vídeo, está ahí diciendo ‘lo siento, lo siento, lo siento’. Pienso que es un malentendido entre él y los chinos, porque en Francia nos enseñan que Mao Zedong es un dictador, obviamente, y supongo que él no quiso ser cruel con su pueblo”. Su información, además, viene de dentro: “Tengo amigos en China y me cuentan por las redes de allí que no están particularmente en contra del vídeo, sino de las palabras que usó Mbappé”. Del entorno del jugador no le ha llamado nadie, ni los agentes ni el Real Madrid, y la ausencia le sorprende. El paso lo dio él. “Le escribí un mensaje por Instagram, pero no me contestó. Imagino que ahora no es el momento”. Lo que de verdad le inquieta no es ese silencio, sino un plan personal en el aire: “Estaba planeando un viaje a China. Espero que no tengan nada contra mí como persona. De momento creo que el meme está bien, pero con el tiempo, si los rivales lo usan demasiado, podría convertirse en algo grande”. La factura del desastre —patrocinadores rotos, contratos caídos, los partidos no televisados en China y el dinero que el Madrid habría dejado de percibir— le queda sencillamente enorme. “No puedo sentir nada especial, porque es tan grande que no entiendo el impacto económico. Primero siento pena, pero no estoy triste. No tengo remordimientos, pero me queda demasiado grande. Es muy, muy grande”. Y ahí aparece la frase que lo retrata entero: “Lo veo todo solo a través de las redes sociales, así que no me parece real. Nadie me ha hablado directamente de las pérdidas. Es como si fuera un episodio de South Park”. Queda la escena que él escribiría si el guion dependiera de su mano, un cara a cara con Mbappé para empezar por lo más difícil. “Querría disculparme, obviamente. Aunque empezara como una broma, nunca quise causar tanto problema, ni económico ni de sentimientos. Se pueden hacer bromas, está bien, pero tengo que asumir que el vídeo creó la situación. De forma indirecta, vale, pero la creó. Le pediría que me perdone”. Y después: “Un café y un apretón de manos”.

articles.title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?
articles.summary: The Africa Cup of Nations will remain on a two-year cycle after the Confederation of African Football performed a U-turn on a decision taken last December.
articles.body:
After a shock announcement 10 months ago that the Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) would be held every four years, the governing body of football on the continent has reversed course.

The Confederation of African Football (Caf) will instead retain the tournament's traditional biennial staging, with its president Patrice Motsepe saying the U-turn was based on "advancing, protecting and promoting" the interests of the African game.

The first indication that the frequency of Afcon was being reconsidered came at Caf's strategy conference in Cape Verde earlier this month.

Questions are now being asked about the decision-making process and what this means for the future of African football.

Why was the planned change controversial?

Afcon has predominantly been held every two years since its first edition in 1957, barring two three-year gaps in the 1960s and one year between the 2012 and 2013 tournaments.

On the eve of the 2025 finals in Morocco, Motsepe announced all that would change from 2028.

The South African said the shift to a four-year cycle was, in part, to help the global calendar "be significantly more synchronised and harmonised".

In recent years Afcon has been staged midway through the European club season, leading to recurring disputes over the release of African players.

Fifa general secretary Mattias Grafstrom was sitting aside Motsepe when the plan was announced, and critics highlighted that the scheduling change favoured football's world governing body more than the African game.

"I think the general sentiment around the continent has been that the two-year cycle has served the continent very well," Football Association of Zambia (Faz) official Sydney Mungala told the BBC.

"The idea of pushing it to a four-year cycle was a bit of a surprise, maybe a concern, to the bulk of the African federations."

Afcon to return to two-year cycle after Caf U-turn

Afcon to be held every four years from 2028

Afcon has developed into Caf's biggest revenue generator, with a profit of $114m (£85m) forecast for Afcon 2025, up from $75m (£56m) for the previous finals in Ivory Coast.

In its stead, an annual Africa Nations League involving all 54 countries on the continent was proposed. Motsepe described the ambition as creating a "world-class competition every year".

The idea was to move beyond Caf's heavy reliance on Afcon and develop a more sustainable commercial model which could support football development.

Yet the last time an ambitious alternative competition took place in Africa, it failed to deliver on its financial promise and was quickly ditched.

The Africa Super League, announced by Caf in 2022 to revolutionise continental club competition, and with projected annual revenues of $200m (£149m), was discontinued after just one edition.

Motsepe later acknowledged that commercial deals fell short of expectations.

"We didn't proceed as quickly because the partners that were giving us money were not giving us the deals we thought we would be happy with," he said.

The decision to move to a four-year cycle was taken at a meeting of Caf's executive committee last December - without being tabled at a general assembly where all member nations are represented.

"These kinds of decisions should be put to the general assembly, they should be debated and discussed for months at a time," Algerian journalist Maher Mezahi told the BBC.

"Afcon is the locomotive by which Caf funds all of its other competitions."

Caf subsequently asked its 54 associations to express a preference between proceeding with the four-year format or retaining the original schedule, and the executive committee eventually voted to restore the status quo.

Motsepe said the decision was in the "best interest of African football" and would contribute to the development and growth of the sport.

He also admitted misgivings about the new Nations League, with concerns it would require "several years" before it could make "the substantial financial and football development contributions" to help the continental game be "self-supporting".

Fifa president Gianni Infantino first publicly proposed holding Afcon every four years in February 2020, an idea Motsepe rejected after he was elected as Caf president 13 months later.

That has not stopped the South African cultivating a close relationship with his counterpart and Infantino's drive to expand the Fifa World Cup to 48 teams - and in the process increase African representation at the tournament - has won him backing across the continent.

Yet the Swiss' position has been under threat since his plan to sell stakes in Fifa's competitions was leaked in July.

Since then Infantino has been busy shoring up his power base ahead of his re-election bid, including at Caf's strategy meeting this month.

"He came to Cape Verde to generate support, And, by and large, Africa gave him that support," Mezahi said.

"But I think they did that in a quid pro quo - they gave him the support in return for some concessions.

"And I think the main concession was the return of the Africa Cup of Nations [to a two-year cycle].

"It shows that Africa is willing to assert its influence and look after its interests, even in the face of the global game's interest."

Infantino says he is backed by 'vast majority'

Does Africa still back Infantino as Fifa president?

Afcon is Caf's financial lifeline, accounting for a substantial share of the governing body's income.

Morocco 2025 was projected to generate $192m (£143m), representing 66% of Caf's total revenue from competitions across men's, women's and age-group football.

For many FAs, Afcon's importance extends far beyond the tournament because they cannot always rely on consistent government or corporate investment.

"We have 11 [Zambian] national teams and only two are partly sponsored by government," Faz official Mungala said.

"The rest have to be supported from the FA's coffers. We actually fund some of these programmes from the support that we get from Caf and Fifa."

The 2027 Afcon is scheduled to be held in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda from 19 June to 17 July next year.

Yet, on a visit to East Africa in September, Motsepe called for a "heightened sense of urgency" in order to make sure stadiums and supporting infrastructure are ready on time.

The next Afcon will be held just one year later in 2028 - a decision Caf made when planning for the switch to a four-year cycle and which it as has decided to stick with.

An announcement on where and exactly when the finals will be held is yet to be made.

Subsequent tournaments will be held in 2031 and 2033 to avoid clashes with the World Cup.

The proposed kick-off date for the Africa Nations League, meanwhile, is September 2029.

Motsepe's latest statement suggests the new competition will also be held every two years - rather than annually as he initially announced last December – but that begs the question of how space will be found for the fixtures to be played in an Afcon year from 2031 onwards.

While debate continues around the game's congested calendar, Caf's U-turn on scheduling has at least protected the tradition of Africa's biggest sporting showcase.

It also exposes, however, the challenge of finding a workable financial model which benefits African football as well as the demands of the global game.

articles.title: 5-Star QB Trae Taylor Reveals Impact of Anthony Colandrea's Return for 2027 on Nebraska Commitment
articles.summary: Anthony Colandrea returning to Nebraska for the 2027 season will have no impact on top quarterback recruit Trae Taylor coming to Lincoln for his freshman year.
articles.body:
Anthony Colandrea returning to Nebraska for the 2027 season will have no impact on top quarterback recruit Trae Taylor coming to Lincoln for his freshman year.

Taylor, a 5-star recruit and No. 1 overall quarterback in the 2027 class, wrote on X that Colandrea coming back "changes absolutely nothing for my commitment" and he looks forward to "coming in and competing and learning" from the entire entire Nebraska quarterback room:

"My phone is blowing up wanting interviews about Ant coming back," Taylor wrote on Friday. "I'll post it here and get back focused on my game tonight. I absolutely love that he is coming back and hope TJ stays I can learn a ton from both. I respect every QB in that room as all of them have been helpful to me already. This changes absolutely nothing for my commitment and I'm 100% locked in. Looking forward to coming in and competing and learning. Hope that answers everyone's questions on where me and my family stand. #GBR sorry I can't do interviews today I just need to lock in on standing bear tonight hope everyone understands."

Colandrea's agency announced on Friday he has agreed to a deal that will keep him with the Cornhuskers for his final year of college eligibility.

This is Colandrea's first season with Nebraska after transferring from UNLV. He has been solid so far with 1,570 yards, 14 touchdowns and six interceptions in seven games.

Taylor has been committed to Nebraska since May 2025. He picked the Huskers over a group of other high-profile programs that includes Michigan, LSU and Texas A&M.

One thing that may have helped Nebraska maintain its advantage over other programs is location. Taylor is currently a senior at Millard South High School in Omaha.

Taylor told ESPN's Eli Lederman at the time of his commitment that his meetings with quarterbacks coach Glenn Thomas helped sell him on Nebraska.

"Sitting down with Coach Thomas and getting into the offense, seeing how he coaches Dylan and how he can prepare me for the next level — I really just can't wait," Taylor told ESPN's Eli Lederman . "For me, it's kind of hard committing too early because I have to wait so long to get there."

Taylor reaffirming his commitment to Nebraska is a huge win for head coach Matt Rhule and his staff. The Cornhuskers currently have the 15th-ranked recruiting class in 2027 with 21 total commits, led by Taylor.

Rhule has Nebraska off to a 5-2 start this season going into Saturday's matchup with Washington in Lincoln.

articles.title: Enric Gallego, 'amo' de casa
articles.standfirst: A sus 40 años se convierte en el único futbolista de las cinco grandes Ligas europeas que asume en exclusiva todos los goles de su equipo como local
articles.summary: A sus 40 años se convierte en el único futbolista de las cinco grandes Ligas europeas que asume en exclusiva todos los goles de su equipo como local
articles.body: El Heliodoro Rodríguez López es patrimonio exclusivo de Enric Gallego. El atacante del Tenerife ha conseguido, a sus 40 años, un registro inédito en el fútbol continental, ya que es el único futbolista de las dos máximas categorías de España, Inglaterra, Italia, Alemania y Francia que ha anotado absolutamente todos los goles conseguidos por su equipo cuando actúa como local. Los números del ariete catalán, líder del Trofeo Pichichi junto al indálico Miguel de la Fuente, describen un monopolio estadístico sin precedentes, ya que Gallego ha anotado los cinco goles suscritos por los blanquiazules en otros tantos partidos celebrados ante su hinchada en lo que va de curso: uno ante Almería, Cádiz y Girona y el doblete frente al Leganés. Ningún otro compañero en el conjunto isleño ha conseguido, por el momento, ayudarle con las tareas domésticas y acompañarlo a la hora de perforar las redes de los adversarios que visitan el Heliodoro. Solo él ha asumido esa producción realizadora en el feudo de los isleños, algo insólito en las principales categorías del Viejo Continente. Esa soberanía absoluta no es una racha pasajera. Si ampliamos el horizonte a todo el año natural, encontramos que el estadio santacrucero es su feudo de caza particular. Los datos dicen que Gallego ha anotado en 12 de las 16 comparecencias que el Tenerife ha disputado como local. Esa regularidad implacable lo corona no solo como el líder del ataque blanquiazul, sino también como el mayor terrateniente del gol de todo el fútbol europeo cuando juega al amparo de sus incondicionales.

La lista es la misma que la del pasado fin de semana ante el Betis. En la convocatoria figuran los futbolistas del filial, Hugo Burcio y Andrés Antañón, en dinámica del primer equipo desde hace varias semanas y contando con minutos de juego. El técnico ha optado por no convocar a los también futbolistas del Celta Fortuna, Milla y Ángel Arcos, habida cuenta del buen número de bajas con las que también cuenta el filial y el importante partido que disputan en la tarde de este sábado, en Balaídos ante el Córdoba.

articles.title: Vallecas recupera su fondo: vía libre para el regreso de 'Bukaneros'
articles.standfirst: El Rayo recibirá al Celta con todo su estadio abierto tras la clausura ante el Elche por la suspensión ante el Athletic
articles.summary: El Rayo recibirá al Celta de Vigo con la presencia de todo su público
articles.body: El fondo de animación vuelve al Estadio de Vallecas. Tras la suspensión del encuentro ante el Athletic Club, que fue castigada con una multa de 6.000 euros al club y el cierre parcial de una parte del Estadio de Vallecas, la afición ubicada en la zona de encima de los vestuarios volverá a alentar a su equipo. Antes del encuentro ante el Elche, un grupo compuesto por la Federación Madrileña de Peñas, diez peñas rayistas y 22 abonados del fondo afectado presentó una demanda a la RFEF por una vulneración de los derechos fundamentales de los aficionados y en la que se exigía que los aficionados que no estuvieron implicados regresaran a sus butacas. Sin embargo, el Tribunal consideró, dada la inmediatez del encuentro ante los ilicitanos, no se podía adoptar la medida de que los aficionados regresaran a sus butacas. El encuentro ante el Elche acabó 0-3 con la peor versión de los de Beñat San José en esta temporada. "Nos han ganado, nos han pintado la cara y ya está”, afirmó Lejeune tras el partido. El defensa francés incidió en la importancia de la falta del fondo de animación donde se encuentran los ultras del equipo. "Esperamos que el próximo sábado contra el Celta estén los Bukaneros con nosotros y nos apoyen", afirmó. Otro que habló sobre ello fue Alemao. “Echamos de menos a Bukaneros. Ellos son como un jugador más o dos o tres. Nos apoyan mucho y nos dan mucha fuerza”, declaró tras el encuentro. Tal y como recalcaron los jugadores, la falta del ‘corazón’ del Estadio de Vallecas se notó dentro del césped. Beñat San José también notó esa falta. “Fue el peor encuentro de la temporada y había un ambiente enrarecido. Si no está toda la familia, no estamos todos a gusto", afirmó antes del encuentro ante el Recreativo de Huelva. En el encuentro de Copa del Rey se vieron alrededor de un centenar de rayistas. Los jugadores agradecieron su presencia acudiendo al córner donde se encontraban y en comuna vivieron esa ‘Vida Pirata’. Algunos por primera vez. Muchos volvieron en coche, otros en tren a la mañana siguiente. Los que volvieron por la red ferroviaria no sabían que vivirían uno de los acontecimientos más desagradables de la historia del país. Alrededor de 50, la mayoría ‘Bukaneros’, como expresaron testigos allí presentes, se bajaron del tren y recorrieron varios kilómetros para ayudar a los afectados. Después de esta solidaria actuación, no hubo respuesta del grupo ni reivindicación de lo sucedido. “No queremos protagonismo”, fue su mensaje. Tanto Beñat San José en la previa del partido ante el Celta, como el club por un comunicado a través de sus redes sociales, agradecieron estos actos a la afición rayista. “Lo hemos comentado en el club y toda la familia rayista nos sentimos muy orgullosos de lo que hicieron. Me emocionó bastante y es un gesto que define valores. Agradecer que lo hicieran por todas las personas que necesitaban ayuda. Dice mucho de ellos", afirmó el técnico vasco. Aunque el clima sea de reconocimiento hacia la afición, cabe recordar que la Agrupación de Peñas del Rayo Vallecano anunció en un comunicado del 23 de octubre que exigían una reunión con la directiva para “certificar que hay una voluntad real de cambio por parte del club”. Esa reunión no se ha producido o no se ha hecho pública. Los últimos acontecimientos (la aceptación de algunas de las peticiones de la afición o el reconocimiento público del club con la labor de los rayistas que ayudaron en el accidente) hacen pensar que la tensión entre directiva y afición podría haber menguado. Sin embargo, durante el partido ante el Celta se volverá a ver cuál es el sentir del Rayismo.

articles.title: London City Lionesses: Eder Maestre explains how his team are succeeding in the WSL ahead of big Man City test
articles.summary: Watch London City Lionesses vs Man City in the WSL on Sunday, live on Sky Sports; kick-off 12pm; watch in-game clips and free match highlights across Sky Sports' digital platforms; buy tickets for the game by searching for the London City Lionesses website
articles.body:
Some questioned how he was going to balance a team of such talent - both incoming and already present - most of whom are used to starting, along with Michele Kang's vision for disruption - smash the traditional big three and qualify for Europe.

And it is so far, so good. The Bromley-based club are third in the WSL with 16 points - already seven ahead of Arsenal - and have proven their summer acquisitions were more than just big names through the door.

So that begs the question - how has Maestre done it?

"It's surprisingly good how fast we were able to assemble a lot of things, considering all the things that we have and trying to understand the different contexts that the players came from," he exclusively told Sky Sports ahead of Sunday's game against Manchester City.

"It's about trying to create strong values to respect the identity we are trying to make. We came from good foundations from the last season, so it's about keep building on that.

"The way we want to play - being aggressive out of possession, trying to recover the ball as soon as possible - is something that is easy to engage the players on because everyone wants to have the ball and to use it to make the chances.

"But the way you can reach that efficiency in games is the other thing that is the most difficult, considering the chemistry that you need to promote between the players. That's why in that overall, I'm very happy."

We cannot talk about London City without mentioning Alexia Putellas. On Monday evening, she picked up a record-equalling third Ballon d'Or - the first for a player at a current WSL club.

Her influence in south-east London is growing by the game. She is the club's top league scorer so far this season and is building passing connections with her team-mates, linking the defence and attack as shown in the pass map below.

"Alexia is Alexia," Maestre said of his captain. "That's why she's able to create that chemistry so quickly with the team surrounding her.

"The way she comes back from the injuries that she had, the way she was pushing, recovering the shape, recovering the feelings to win that third Ballon d'Or shows everybody how she's striving every day to be a better player.

"That energy and leadership that she has, this attention to the details, it helps everybody to push. It's a privilege having these kind of players in the squad, not only for the player that they are.

"She is also a mirror where the young players can see themselves, to understand what is the price to reach that target. It's not about deciding, you have to pay the bill and she represents how difficult it is having the consistency that she has."

Another talent flying under the radar is Danielle van de Donk . The midfielder was injured for much of last season but has made a triumphant return this year, already notching up eight goal involvements in eight appearances in all competitions.

"She suffered a lot last season due to the injuries that she had," Maestre said. "It's so frustrating for a player that brings energy to the team, to the team-mates. Hopefully this season, she's in very good shape and she's performing very well.

"In the game, she represents perfectly the identity that this team wants to have, so I'm very happy having her involved. And when she's on the bench, the way she can lead, the energy that she brings to every part of the process is amazing. It's a complete pleasure watching her being able to bring her best to the team."

'Beating a top-three team the next step'

London City will need to draw on all of their experience and success this season when they face unbeaten Manchester City on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

The Lionesses are matching the WSL champions in many overall metrics this season, but have never beaten a traditional 'top-three' team. By Maestre's own admission, winning these games has to be the next step in their development.

If they do so this weekend, London City go level on points with Man City and Chelsea - however briefly - and they surely have to be considered serious title contenders.

"We are moving forward, making good checks, reaching big results against teams like Tottenham playing away, but one that we need to fix is being able to win these kind of teams," Maestre said.

"We are going to have the best test we can have so far because Man City are the ones that won the competition last season.

"If we can show everybody that we are ready to face them while respecting our identity and through that, reaching a good performance and being able to win, it's a very good step to keep pushing, to keep showing everybody that we are here for that [top] position in the standings.

"So many coaches explain how difficult it is creating a winning project and it takes time. It's a consequence of repeating every time those winning behaviours to try to create that strength. It's not about having one, two, three good games.

"The big teams are big teams because they had the consistency to be there a lot of times. That's why it's not about reaching, it's about having enough consistency to keep the reach that you can achieve in one moment. That's why we must be humble."

The stats also paint a positive picture. London City have scored eight goals in the opening 30 minutes of WSL matches this season - the most in the league - while Man City's defensive numbers are on shaky ground.

The WSL champions have conceded nine goals in seven WSL games this season - over twice as many as at the same stage in 2025/26 (4). It is their worst defensive start to a league campaign since 2021/22.

They say numbers don't lie, but Maestre is not using them as a free pass to the top of the WSL this weekend.

"Every game is different," he reflected. "Sometimes it's about a lucky or unlucky situation and Man City are doing the same things that they were doing last season.

"This competition is very tough, so everyone can punish everybody, so this humble mentality has to be one of our strong values to keep pushing and to have this consistency.

"We must push as we did in the games before with all the belief that we can reach that performance that we expect to have, that result that we are dreaming that we can have.

"If they are not successful in and out of possession, we will be there to take advantage of that, but we cannot expect that they are going to concede something because we are going to be wrong."

London City have won their last five home WSL games - only Man City having more (16) - and Maestre wants the home support to be a key part of any performance.

"We are really aware of the importance of the game that we have ahead and we are going to push for the win, respecting the identity that we were trying to build since the first day here.

"That's why we are going to need their energy from the stands, because we are going to be in tough moments. If they can be player number 12, we are going to be closer to the performance and the scoring that we are looking for."

articles.body: No hubo sorpresa en Konya. El Galatasary de Osimhen goleó 0-4 al Konyaspor y mantiene intacto su liderato en Turquía. Rafael Leao, que no había arrancado bien el curso y ya recibía críticas, anotó su primer gol como futbolista del Galatasaray... de penalti. No hubo debate y a la media hora de partido el 'Galata' ya ganaba 0-2. Osimhen y Akgun lideraron el camino del triunfo mientras que Batrakov y Leao lo sentenciaron en la segunda parte. El Galatasaray de Okan Buruk, que viene de ganar el derbi ante Fenerbahçe (2-1) en un duelo marcado por las tánganas y los enfrentamientos entre equipos, ya aventaja en cinco puntos al segundo clasificado, el sorprendente Amedspor. Sin embargo, los campeones tienen un partido más que sus perseguidores.

articles.title: Milan's chance, Fiorentina Serie B-bound, sack risk? 5️⃣ on Serie A round 10
articles.summary: With barely any time to recover from the midweek fixtures, Serie A returns tomorrow for a 10th round packed with intriguing storylines.Watch every Serie BKT...
articles.body:
With barely any time to recover from the midweek fixtures, Serie A returns tomorrow for a 10th round packed with intriguing storylines.

Two heavyweight clashes, one between fallen giants, intriguing relegation battles and meetings between struggling sides: here are the main talking points of the round.

⚠️ Allegri and Spalletti: who turns things around and who falls apart?

Juventus and Napoli have collected 14 points in 9 games . That is not even enough for a European spot, with Frosinone occupying one three points ahead. Both teams are 11 points behind Inter and Lazio and desperately need to turn things around.

They head into the game in different circumstances, though. Napoli have picked up 7 points against Bodo/Glimt, Roma and Monza, while Juventus suffered a dismal defeat to Genoa on Wednesday. Both coaches know that a defeat would put them under serious scrutiny , while a win could provide the turning point they so badly want.

🤔 Are Inter really in better shape than Milan?

The league leaders head into the Milan derby sitting top and holding a 7-point lead in the table over the Rossoneri. But all that glitters is not gold. Their 9 points from the last 3 games across the Champions League and Serie A are beyond dispute, but the performances have been far from brilliant.

Amorim's team suffered a heavy defeat to Bologna at San Siro and appear to be badly affected by injuries. Bouncing back against a top club will not be easy, but this huge clash is also a chance to send a message to the rest of the league.

🤩 Will Frosinone-Torino be the best game of the round?

What more is there to say about Frosinone? The league's second-best attack , first for first-half goals, and counter-pressing numbers worthy of a European giant: Massimiliano Alvini's newly promoted side are a joy to watch.

Torino do not reach those heights, but they are a team with a clear identity and style of play. Last year in Serie B, Ignazio Abate made life difficult for Frosinone with his Juve Stabia side, losing 1-0 but creating plenty of chances. Another wide-open match looks likely.

🏆 Can Palladino secure European football?

10 points in 5 games: an outstanding return that has erased the terrible start to the season under Domenico Tedesco. Raffaele Palladino kept Fiorentina in the Conference League two years ago and repeated the feat at Atalanta last year.

By the club management's own admission, Bologna did not start the season with that kind of target. If this run continues, however, nothing is impossible. The Monza game will be a test of maturity for the Rossoblù, who could continue closing the gap on the upper reaches of the table.

😱 Is Sassuolo-Fiorentina a relegation battle?

The question goes beyond the 90 minutes. The table currently says yes, but nobody could have predicted it at the start of the season. Alberto Aquilani made a superb start, beating Juve and holding Milan, but has now become bogged down. The Neroverdi have conceded 22 goals , giving them the worst defensive record in Serie A.

Unlike Sassuolo, Fiorentina's false dawn came later. After Grosso's disastrous start, Paolo Vanoli picked up two wins and a draw and looked set to climb the table. Instead, the Viola are in the relegation zone on 5 points and risk reliving last year's nightmare .

articles.title: Arizona vs. Texas Tech prediction: One fatal flaw that could decide everything
articles.summary: A preseason College Football Playoff contender could be on upset alert again this week.
articles.body:
A critical Big 12 matchup tees off in this weekend's college football action as Arizona and Texas Tech meet in a matchup of AP top 25 ranked rivals.

Both have one loss and sit in a tie for second place in the competitive Big 12 standings. Texas Tech just took a surprise loss at Cincinnati and Arizona is on an impressive five-game win streak.

Whoever loses this one could see their College Football Playoff ambitions vanish into thin air. Who has the ultimate advantage?

Arizona has the passing-game firepower to make this a competitive matchup, but the Wildcats need to turn that strength into sustained offensive production.

Noah Fifita leads an offense averaging 310.9 passing yards per game, ninth-best nationally. And this offense is third in FBS converting almost 55 percent of its third downs.

Texas Tech is third-worst in the Big 12 against the pass and second-worst with 16 touchdowns allowed. Those numbers suggest the Wildcats can move the chains against this defense.

The key remains protecting Fifita, establishing a running game to keep the Tech defense honest, and critically avoiding turnovers.

Defensively, Arizona also needs to continue its recent success against the run. It held Iowa State to just 52 rushing yards in a 39-3 victory last week.

Controlling the ground game forces the Red Raiders to throw the ball, something they're not doing all that consistently.

Balancing out this offense is crucial for the Red Raiders. Surprisingly, they rank in the bad half of the Big 12 in total offensive and defensive efficiency. The good news is they can run the ball moderately well, averaging 190 yards per game and 5 yards per carry.

Running effectively helps Texas Tech control the tempo, keep Noah Fifita and Arizona's potent passing attack on the sideline, and create more manageable situations for quarterback Will Hammond.

Texas Tech needs to consider giving backup quarterback Tommy Castellanos more opportunities. Hammond has struggled – 6 TDs, 6 INTs – while the guy behind him on the depth chart introduces a kind of mobility that is harder to defend.

The one potential fatal flaw Texas Tech could expose this weekend is Arizona's vulnerability to interior pass pressure. That's an area where the Red Raiders' pass rush is still pretty good.

Arizona has allowed 17 sacks this season, ranking third-worst in the Big 12. Tech's interior pass rush could force Fifita to move off his spot and make decisions before his receivers finish their routes.

If Texas Tech generates pressure without blitzing heavily, it can keep extra defenders in coverage and make Arizona work much harder for completions.

Arizona is averaging 311 passing yards per game, while the Red Raiders are allowing 266. That's a significant opportunity for Fifita to expose a defense that showed real structural vulnerability in the loss to Cincinnati.

The Wildcats also have better defensive numbers, allowing just 16 points per game. The Red Raiders can run the ball well at home, but Arizona's passing efficiency and defensive consistency give it a path to a very real upset.

The Big Lead prediction: Arizona 30, Texas Tech 27
